children: A group and several states opposed to the federal government's efforts to reschedule marijuana to a Schedule III substance from Schedule I are asking a DEA judge to allow more testimony and discovery in a hearing on the matter.

"The Tribunal should also request supplemental briefing from the parties to address whether HHS’s lack of internal written policies contributed to an evaluation of marijuana that departed from prior agency practice," Smart Approaches to Marijuana, along with Idaho, Indiana, and Nebraska, argue.

The motion, filed Tuesday, references a September GAO report on DEA scheduling decisions. That document was initially not included in the hearing, but the DEA, in its Tuesday motion, said it is deferring to the judge on that issue.
However, the DEA added that it does not want more briefings on the report's impact on rescheduling, according to
The agency contends that the report "does not present any new evidence salient to the issue before this Tribunal."
DEA Chief Administrative Law Judge Derek Julius has asked the DEA to respond to the opposition's motion by Oct. 21.
The report's release led Julius to
the hearing in late September to see if the DEA was amenable to including the report in the hearing.

title: Marijuana rescheduling opponents ask judge for additional briefings
